deep.reconstruction:
Setting: (M, dm) is a measure space and f is a measurable function. phi_f is the decreasing rearrangement of |f| (or of a real f) on ]0,|M|[, and mu_f is its distribution measure. The previous page defined Phi_f(t)=∫_0^t phi_f, Psi_f(t)=∫_0^t log phi_f and Delta_f(t)=exp Psi_{|f|}(t). It also proved the submultiplicativity Psi_{fg} ≤ Psi_f+Psi_g, i.e. Delta_{fg}(t) ≤ Delta_f(t)Delta_g(t). That is the continuous analogue of Weyl/Horn multiplicative majorization of singular numbers.

This page does three things.

(i) Full determinant (12). Grothendieck sets Delta(f)=Delta_{|f|}(|M|)=exp ∫_M log|f| dm, the geometric mean. It is defined in [0,+∞[ as soon as log^+|f| is integrable. He notes that Delta has the properties of a (multiplicative) determinant: (13) Delta(fg)=Delta(f)Delta(g) and Delta(1)=1. This is exactly the commutative case of the Fuglede–Kadison determinant (Annals 1952) for a von Neumann algebra L^∞(M) with trace ∫. If |M|≠1 one gets the unnormalised version, Delta(λ)=λ^{|M|}.

(ii) Regularised determinant of 1+f.
- If |M|<∞, rearrangement commutes with adding a constant: (14) phi_{1+f}=1+phi_f on [0,|M|].
- If |M|=∞ and f ≥ 0, phi_{1+f} does not exist, because {1+f>s} has infinite measure for s<1.
- He therefore defines directly (15) Delta_{1+f}(t)=exp ∫_0^t log(1+phi_f(s)) ds. This is legitimate whenever Phi_f is finite (phi_f integrable near 0), since 0 ≤ log(1+x) ≤ x.
- He checks coherence with (9) and with (16) Delta_{1+f}(|M|)=Delta(1+f) when |M|<∞.

In the infinite-measure case this is the commutative germ of a Fredholm-type determinant det(1+T) for T in L^1 of a semifinite (II_∞) trace.

(iii) Inverse problem. Let mu be a positive measure on R* with finite tails ∫_a^∞ dmu<∞ (a>0), and let "mu" be its total mass (possibly +∞). Then there is a unique decreasing phi on ]0,"mu"[ with mu_phi=mu, and phi>0 iff mu is carried by R*_+. In other words, every such measure is the distribution of a unique decreasing function, its own rearrangement.

Purpose: these are preparatory notes for Grothendieck's Séminaire Bourbaki exposé 113 (1955), 'Réarrangements de fonctions et inégalités de convexité dans les algèbres de von Neumann munies d'une trace'. They develop the commutative model of the singular-value function, Ky Fan/Weyl-type inequalities and Fuglede–Kadison determinants before transferring them to traced von Neumann algebras.
errors: (12)/(13): calling Delta 'a determinant' is only literally right for |M|=1. In general Delta is a power, det^{|M|}, of the normalized determinant. The marginal word Grothendieck inserted seems to acknowledge this.

(15) is written with log|1+phi_f| and with 0≤|t|≤|M|. For real (not necessarily positive) f, 1+phi_f can vanish or be negative and the log is no longer positive. The claim that 'log(1+phi_f) is a positive function' presupposes f ≥ 0 (or the use of phi_{|f|}).

In the case |M|=∞, the existence of the full Delta_{1+f}(∞) needs ∫_0^∞ log(1+phi_f)<∞, roughly f in L^1. Grothendieck only states the local integrability near 0; the statement 'donc sur tout intervalle' covers only finite intervals.
The inverse-problem statement is sloppy about the interval: 'R*_+' versus ']0,M[' versus ']0,"mu"['. The marginal note '"mu"<+∞ !' shows he noticed that the finite-mass case must be singled out.

missed.claim: Grothendieck extends the determinant to 1+f on an infinite measure space via rearrangements, a commutative prototype of det(1+T) for trace-class T in a II_∞ algebra. The submultiplicativity of the previous page makes this a natural route to a Lidskii/Fredholm determinant theory in semifinite algebras, which appeared only in the 1980s.
missed.quote: On pourra donc définir (15) Δ_{1+f}(t) = exp∫_0^t log|1+φ_f(s)| ds
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Mostly historical. It shows Grothendieck anticipating the Delta_t / generalized s-number determinant machinery (Fack–Kosaki) and semifinite Fredholm determinants. These are, however, natural extensions, and the noncommutative step is not on this page.

deep.surprise_reason: These are routine commutative rearrangement facts, but they deliberately pair Fuglede–Kadison determinants with partial determinants Delta_f(t) and a regularised det(1+f) for infinite measure. That anticipates later semifinite-algebra determinant work (Fack–Kosaki, Brown). It is likely partly reflected in his 1955 Bourbaki exposé, so the novelty is modest.
transcription_corrections: The word inserted above 'déterminant' in line 'Δ jouit des propriétés d'un ... déterminant' is hard to read. It may be 'multiplicatif'/'multiple de'; the reading is uncertain.
(12) reads Δ(f) = Δ_{|f|}(|M|) = exp∫_M log|f| dm (the integration variable is dm, the measure of M, not dμ).
Marginal note at the bottom left reads approximately 'Le bon ... "μ" < +∞ !' together with ']0,"μ"['.
